doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Baton Rouge bands: same style as New Orleans, parades and ballyhoo wagons
summary: The Baton Rouge bands played lawn parties, dances and funeral parades, and advertised dances from horse-drawn wagons stopping at saloons.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: that time, was, was the kind of music they played about the same as in New Orleans? Same style?

Exactly the same, yeah. Exactly the same? Oh, yeah. That was really one of the good bands. What kind of places did you play with the band? They played lawn parties, dances, parades. Did they have parades in Baton Rouge? Oh, yeah. They had them funeral parades in Baton Rouge, just like they had in New Orleans. Oh, yeah. Did you hear them play any of them? Exactly. Sure. But the thing I can remember the best is when those bands used to ballyhoo would dance. Like,
they was going to have a dance at night, they would, they would be on one of those, uh, wagons,

you know? Was it, was it, uh, like a truck or with horses? Horses. Horses. Horses. Not, not, no, no truck, no. They had very few trucks in those days. No, and those cats would stop in front of every saloon. Yeah. And the saloon that'd give them the most drinks, they would play there the longest. They'd bring the drinks out or would they invite them? They'd bring them out. They'd bring them out? Sometimes they'd bring them out and sometimes the guys would have a little short intermission and go in and take a couple of shots and come back out and play. But they had exactly the same deal, that second line deal that they had in New Orleans. No, no different. Because I used to do the same thing in New Orleans. I took lessons from Piku. Did you? I didn't bother. Piku and my father was good friends. Oh. Was your father a musician? Yeah. Played a little E-flat cornet.
